title: Vibrations All Around
description: Echo Bot 🤖 scans the academy for hidden vibrations. Spot how different instruments make sound to earn the first bell fragment.

content.value: Musical instruments are machines for making controlled vibrations. Even though they look very different, each one works by vibrating some part of itself.

TYPE          EXAMPLE          WHAT VIBRATES
String        🎸 guitar, sitar   the strings
Wind          🎺 flute, trumpet  the air column inside
Percussion    🥁 drum, tabla     the stretched membrane
Metal         🔔 bell, cymbal    the metal itself
In a guitar or sitar, plucking a string makes it vibrate, and the vibration produces sound. A tighter or shorter string vibrates faster and gives a different note — that's how musicians play tunes.

In a flute, blowing makes the AIR COLUMN inside vibrate. In a drum or tabla, striking makes the stretched skin vibrate. The vibrating part always sets the surrounding air moving, and that carries the sound to your ears.
A vibrating object is called a SOURCE of sound. In every instrument, find the source — the part that shakes — and you've found where the sound is born.
Key Takeaway: All instruments make sound by vibrating a part of themselves — strings, air columns, membranes, or metal. The vibrating part is the source of the sound.

quiz.question: In a flute, what actually vibrates to make the sound?
quiz.explain: Blowing across a flute makes the air column inside it vibrate, producing the sound.

quiz.question: In a drum, the sound comes from the vibrating…
quiz.explain: Striking a drum makes its stretched membrane vibrate, which produces sound.

quiz.question: The vibrating part of an instrument is called the…
quiz.explain: The object that vibrates and makes the sound is the source.
